summary: Quick frontend-only retest of 2 player issues (375x667, web preview, channel A&E FHD H.265). HIGH fix (overlay waits 15s): PASS for the first channel. The overlay went away at ~6s, when video.readyState hit 4 (it used to take 15s). NEW REGRESSION after Next: the overlay never shows for the new channel. player.status is still the old channel's 'readyToPlay' right after replaceAsync resolves, so markPlaying() runs immediately. The spinner is gone at t=0 while readyState=0 until ~8s. MEDIUM fix (controls auto-hide): PARTIAL. Controls stay visible while phase=loading (0-6s, OK). But once phase=playing they hide at t=10s while the <video> is actually PAUSED (paused=true, currentTime=0), leaving a black screen with no UI. RCA: the video events were play@34ms, abort@42ms (load() from replace aborts the play), then canplay@6.7s. After that, nothing calls play() again: markPlaying() skips play() because player.playing is stale-true, and isPlaying stays true. Calling video.play() by hand after canplay played the stream fine (currentTime moved 0 -> 6.2s, A&E picture visible). So the stream works; the player logic just never restarts playback.

ui_bugs.issue: On web the video never starts playing. play() is called and then aborted by the source load (events: play@34, abort@42, loadstart@45, canplay@6736). markPlaying() only calls play() when !player.playing, but player.playing is stale-true, so play() is never sent again. Result: video paused at 0s, overlay hidden, controls hidden 4s later, black screen. Calling video.play() by hand after canplay works.

Regression. After Next, player.status still holds the previous channel's 'readyToPlay' when replaceAsync resolves, so markPlaying() runs at t=0. The loading overlay never appears for the new channel (readyState stayed 0 until ~8s), and the controls hide at 4s on a black screen.
reallyPlaying relies on isPlaying, which is stale-true on web while the <video> is paused. Controls hid at t=10s with paused=true and currentTime=0.

action_items: In markPlaying(), always call player.play() (remove the `if (!player.playing)` guard). The first play() is aborted by the source load on web, and player.playing stays stale-true.

Do not trust player.status right after replaceAsync: it may be the previous source's 'readyToPlay'. Options: save prevStatus before replace and only markPlaying immediately if prevStatus !== 'readyToPlay'. Or better, listen to expo-video's 'sourceLoad' event (or poll status every ~500ms after fresh) to detect that the new source is ready.
Gate the controls auto-hide on real playback progress, e.g. the 'timeUpdate' event with currentTime advancing (set player.timeUpdateEventInterval) instead of isPlaying, which goes stale.
critical_code_review_comments: player.tsx:82: the immediate status check after replaceAsync reads stale status from the previous source when you change channel.
player.tsx:56: the `!player.playing` guard prevents recovery from an aborted play().

Status 'readyToPlay' from the old source carries over when replaceAsync resolves, so the new-channel overlay is skipped.
